$comment: D-CSUBSET-NULLPTR-T-DECLARABLE: the runtime witness for a C23 `nullptr_t` OBJECT (§6.2.5 — an object type with exactly one value and the size, alignment and representation of `void *`). exitCode 42 = 1|2|4|8|16 (=31) + sizeof(o)=8 + 3. Each bit is a distinct behaviour that FAILED TO COMPILE at 301e2a63 with I_NullptrTypeInMir + I_StoreValueTypeMismatch, while gcc 13.3.0 (-std=c2x) and clang 18.1.3 (-std=c23), probed separately, both compile and run it: 1 = the object and its initializing store; 2 = a same-type copy (load of a nullptr_t slot, store into another); 4 = the one-way conversion to `void *`; 8 = a comparison against an OPAQUE volatile-sourced address, so the release arm witnesses a genuine RUNTIME pointer compare rather than a fold; 16 = the C23 6.3.2.4p2 truth value (false); the +8 is the WIDTH, which is what makes a projection to anything narrower than a pointer red. The semantic tier keeps `nullptr_t` a DISTINCT identity (a `_Generic` over it must not select the `void *` arm); only the representation is projected. The `release` arm (shippedPipeline, zero-drift) proves the optimizer preserves all of it over the new Ptr-shaped MIR.
